item.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
item.description: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. item.title: Follow-up: 2026 papers are finally in the topic pages, and we made ICML / CVPR / ICLR 2026 "newspapers"[P]
item.description: A few weeks ago I posted the topic pages we built from 10 years of ICML/NeurIPS/ICLR/CVPR/AAAI papers. A bunch of you pointed out the obvious gap: the benchmark records and ablations stopped at 2025. That's fixed now. We've pulled results out of about 101k full texts (it was 79k when I posted), roughly a million "tried X, got Y" findings. 2026 is mostly covered: almost all of ICML, CVPR and AAAI, and about 4.1k of 5.4k ICLR papers. NeurIPS 2026 is only a bit over half done, mostly because a lot of the PDFs aren't public yet.
